# MITRE ATT&CK coverage

<!-- Generated by scripts/build-coverage.ps1 on 2026-08-03T02:19:01.8716928Z. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every row below is derived from an evidence bundle in `evidence/`. A technique is
listed as covered only because a scenario produced a `detected` result for it, never
because a rule exists.

## What this matrix does not mean

- Coverage of a technique here means **one** specific behaviour was detected once, in
  one lab, on one host. It does not mean the technique is covered in general; each
  technique has many procedures and this lab exercises one.
- Detection here says nothing about whether the rule would survive an attacker who is
  actively trying to evade it.
- A benign marker run is the weakest possible test, because the same person wrote the
  rule and the activity meant to trigger it. Only an externally defined Atomic Red Team
  test removes that circularity, which is why the two are counted separately below.
